original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dcurve(n), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by n points lying on a constant-degree algebraic curve in the plane when the curve contains neither a line nor a circle.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 5: the paper defines Dcurve(n) as the minimum number of distinct distances spanned by n points on a constant-degree algebraic curve γ in R^2, under the condition that γ contains no line or circle, and then asks for the asymptotic value of Dcurve(n). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct official target almost exactly: it uses the singular one-curve quantity Dcurve(n), asks for an asymptotic answer, restricts the points to a constant-degree algebraic curve in the plane, and excludes the exceptional line and circle cases. This matches Section 3, Problem 5, rather than the neighboring curve-incidence question in Section 2 or the later bipartite two-curve quantity Dcurves(m,n) in Section 5. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: The paper's ambient space is R^2, and the distances are ordinary Euclidean distances.
Dcurve(n) should be explicitly defined as a minimum over all n-point sets P and all admissible curves γ, rather than left as an informal symbol.
The admissible curve γ is a real plane algebraic curve, i.e. the zero set of a polynomial of degree bounded by an absolute constant independent of n.
The exclusion applies to the curve γ itself: γ must contain no line and no circle.
The distances counted are those determined by unordered pairs of distinct points of P.
Asymptotic value here means the order of growth of Dcurve(n) as n → ∞, i.e. up to Θ(·)-equivalence.
refined_question: Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by unordered pairs of distinct points of a finite set P ⊂ R^2. For n ∈ N, define Dcurve(n) := min D(P), where the minimum is taken over all n-point sets P contained in a real plane algebraic curve γ ⊂ R^2 of degree bounded by an absolute constant, under the restriction that γ contains no line and no circle. Determine the asymptotic growth of Dcurve(n) as n → ∞.
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Section 3, Problem 5. The sentence immediately before it introduces Dcurve(n) with precisely the one-curve, planar, constant-degree, no-line/no-circle hypotheses, and Problem 5 then asks for its asymptotic value. So the draft needed only the formal definition of D(P), the minimization over P and γ, and the explicit Euclidean/R^2 setting to become fully stand-alone. I did not broaden it to Section 2, Problem 4, which is about how many points of a near-optimal set may lie on a curve, nor to Section 5, Problem 17, which is the bipartite two-curve quantity Dcurves(m,n). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
